title: What If Campi Flegrei, Naples' Supervolcano, Erupted?

scenes.text: There is a supervolcano beside Naples, and the ground above it keeps rising. What if it erupted?
Campi Flegrei is Europe's largest active caldera, about 14 kilometers across, with 24 craters. A third of it lies under the bay.
About 500,000 people live in its red zone. The evacuation plan needs roughly 72 hours, on roads locals fear can't cope.
Civil Protection rates a small or average eruption as 95 percent likely. The last one, in 1538, built a 133-meter cone in eight days.
Even that would threaten about 15,000 buildings in the high-risk zone, including 125 schools, in a region far denser than in 1538.
The ground has risen up to 10 centimeters a year, with over a thousand tremors a month in 2023. Scientists say eruption isn't inevitable.
